title: Class 9 Maths, All Chapters: Term 2 (Part II)
subtitle: Start here for Term 2. One roadmap for each chapter of NCERT Ganita Manjari, Grade 9 Part II (Chapters 9 to 14), written for students who find maths hard. This page shows the one idea in each chapter, what each needs first, and the thread that runs through them all.

links.label: The whole year: Term 1 and Term 2

topics.desc:
**Goal:** know how the Part II chapter roadmaps fit together, and where to begin.

Each chapter of the NCERT Ganita Manjari, Grade 9 Part II textbook has its own roadmap, written for students who find maths hard. This page connects them. Part I (Chapters 1 to 8) has its own start page.

children.label: How to use these roadmaps
children.desc:
- **One roadmap per chapter.** Open a chapter below, then follow its own steps.
- **Every chapter starts with *Check yourself*.** Two minutes, a few questions. It tells you which small skills to fix before the chapter itself.
- **Solid boxes are the core path.** Dashed boxes are optional: stories, extra puzzles and the *When you're ready* challenge questions.
- **Every chapter ends with a section for teachers and parents**, with a lesson plan, common mistakes and a 5-minute exit ticket.
- **Progress is saved per chapter** on this device. Mark steps **Done** inside each chapter's roadmap.

children.label: About this roadmap
children.desc:
**What it is.** The starting page for Term 2: 6 roadmaps, one for each chapter of the NCERT textbook *Ganita Manjari*, Grade 9 Part II (Chapters 9 to 14).

**Who it is for.** Class 9 students who find maths hard, or who have fallen behind and want to catch up. It also works for revision, and for the teachers and parents helping them: the last milestone is written for adults.

**What this page does.** It shows the one idea in each chapter, what each chapter needs first, and the thread that runs through them. It does not teach the chapters itself: open a chapter to start.

**How the chapter roadmaps work.** Each one starts by fixing the basic skills it needs, shows every calculation, gives practice with hidden answers, keeps harder material in an optional *When you're ready* milestone, and ends with a section for teachers and parents. The 6 lesson plans add up to 35 periods.

**Can you trust it?** Every number in the worked examples and answers was checked by a computer program, and every picture was drawn specially for this roadmap. All the examples are original, so students still get fresh practice from the textbook itself. If you spot a mistake, use **Report a problem** at the top of the page.

**Not official.** This is a free, independent resource. It follows the NCERT textbook but is not made or endorsed by NCERT or CBSE. It is shared under the **CC BY-SA 4.0** licence: you may copy, adapt and share it, including in your school, as long as you credit it and share your version the same way.

children.label: The thread through Part II
children.desc:
Part II keeps reaching back into Part I.

- **Chapter 9** is about reasoning: 'if ... then', converses and counterexamples. These tools come back in Chapter 12.
- **Chapter 10** combines averages: Chapter 7's fractions and percentages, used on real data.
- **Chapter 11** writes exact recipes, and finds the greatest common divisor (last seen when simplifying fractions in Chapter 3) the fast way.
- **Chapter 12** proves facts about quadrilaterals by cutting them into triangles, and checks their converses (Chapter 9).
- **Chapter 13** brings Chapters 1 and 2 together: points on a grid, and a start plus a jump becomes a line with a slope.
- **Chapter 14** is Chapter 6 in three dimensions: fence or floor becomes wrapping or filling.

A student who sees the thread finds each new chapter a little smaller than it looks.

children.label: Which chapter needs which
children.desc:
- **Chapter 9:** multiples, factors and squares (fixed inside the chapter).
- **Chapter 10:** averages, percentages and ratios (fixed inside the chapter).
- **Chapter 11:** divisors and remainders (fixed inside the chapter).
- **Chapter 12:** converses from Chapter 9; triangle angles and congruence from Chapter 5.
- **Chapter 13:** plotting from Chapter 1; 'start plus jump' from Chapter 2.
- **Chapter 14:** circle formulas from Chapter 6; Pythagoras.

children.label: For teachers: pacing Part II
children.desc:
The 6 lesson plans add up to **35 periods** (Part I adds 66 more):
- Chapter 9, Propositions and Converses: 4 periods
- Chapter 10, Combining Data: 6 periods
- Chapter 11, Algorithms: 5 periods
- Chapter 12, Quadrilaterals: 6 periods
- Chapter 13, Linear Equations in Two Variables: 7 periods
- Chapter 14, Surface Area and Volume: 7 periods

**A suggestion:** Chapter 9 is short and has almost no calculation. It is a good chapter for a student who struggles with arithmetic to do well in, and its reasoning tools make Chapter 12 easier.

Each plan leaves space for revision. Keep the optional challenge milestones for students who are ready.

topics.label: Chapter 9: Propositions and Converses
topics.desc:
**The one idea:** An 'if ... then' statement only works one way: turn it round and check again. One counterexample is enough to show a statement is false.

**Needs first:** Multiples, factors and square numbers. The roadmap's *Start here* covers them.

Textbook chapter: *Propositions and their Converses*. The roadmap has 27 steps, 18 of them on the core path.
